gen_ai.input.messages.content:
You read a task before any planning and list what its key names and terms could mean.

# Task
A carrier must move 10 loads today using up to 4 trucks. Each load goes on exactly one truck. A truck that carries any load costs its fixed daily cost plus its per-mile rate times the total miles of its loads. Constraints per truck: total weight ≤ weight capacity, total miles ≤ mileage limit.
Loads (weight lb, miles): L1 18000, 220; L2 12500, 340; L3 22000, 150; L4 9000, 410; L5 15500, 95; L6 7000, 280; L7 20500, 190; L8 11000, 365; L9 14000, 120; L10 8500, 255.
Trucks (capacity lb, mileage limit, fixed $/day, $/mile): A 45000, 1100, 350, 2.10; B 45000, 1100, 350, 2.10; C 30000, 1100, 500, 1.85; D 26000, 900, 275, 2.45.
Find the minimum-cost assignment. Give the total cost, each truck's loads, weight and miles, and show how you know it is optimal. Deliver an .xlsx with the plan and the cost calculation as formulas.

# What we know about the user (read-only context; may be empty)
None given.

# What to do
Find the words that decide what the task is about and could be read more than one way: names of organisations,
places, products and people; abbreviations and acronyms; and likely voice-input errors (letters spoken as words,
such as "P and W" for "PNW", or words that sound alike). Leave out words whose meaning is not in doubt.
For each such entity give every plausible reading, a one-line justification, and a confidence from 0 to 1 (the
confidences of one entity's readings add up to at most 1). A reading that fits what we know about the user is more
likely. If nothing in the task is in doubt, return an empty list.

# Your answer
The list of entities, each with the words as written in the task and its readings (reading, a one-line why, and a
confidence from 0 to 1). An empty list when nothing in the task is in doubt.


Reply with only one JSON object that matches this JSON schema, nothing else:
{"properties": {"rationale": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "optional, at most two sentences"}, "entities": {"description": "empty when nothing in the task is in doubt", "items": {"properties": {"entity": {"description": "the words as written in the task", "type": "string"}, "readings": {"items": {"properties": {"reading": {"type": "string"}, "why": {"description": "one line", "type": "string"}, "confidence": {"description": "0 to 1; one entity's readings add up to at most 1", "type": "number"}}, "required": ["reading", "why", "confidence"], "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false}, "type": "array"}}, "required": ["entity", "readings"], "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false}, "type": "array"}}, "required": ["rationale", "entities"], "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false}

gen_ai.input.messages.content:
You decide, before a team is planned for a task, whether the planner needs facts from the web to plan it well.

# Task
A carrier must move 10 loads today using up to 4 trucks. Each load goes on exactly one truck. A truck that carries any load costs its fixed daily cost plus its per-mile rate times the total miles of its loads. Constraints per truck: total weight ≤ weight capacity, total miles ≤ mileage limit.
Loads (weight lb, miles): L1 18000, 220; L2 12500, 340; L3 22000, 150; L4 9000, 410; L5 15500, 95; L6 7000, 280; L7 20500, 190; L8 11000, 365; L9 14000, 120; L10 8500, 255.
Trucks (capacity lb, mileage limit, fixed $/day, $/mile): A 45000, 1100, 350, 2.10; B 45000, 1100, 350, 2.10; C 30000, 1100, 500, 1.85; D 26000, 900, 275, 2.45.
Find the minimum-cost assignment. Give the total cost, each truck's loads, weight and miles, and show how you know it is optimal. Deliver an .xlsx with the plan and the cost calculation as formulas.

# What to decide
Planning needs the web only when the shape of the plan depends on something a planner cannot know, or may know
wrongly or out of date:
- which source, agency, dataset, API or document publishes what the task needs, or whether it exists at all;
- a current fact that decides which steps or tools are needed (a recent rule, release, product, price list or event);
- what a name or term in the task refers to, when the readings above leave it open.

Do not search for the task's answer, or for figures the team will look up while it works: the team has web tools of
its own. Most tasks need no search before planning.

# Output
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"need_search": true or false, "why": "<one sentence>",
 "queries": [{"query": "<web search query>", "reason": "<what the plan needs from it>"}, ...]}

At most 4 queries, each a short web search query under 200 characters. A query goes to an
outside search service: write it in general words, never with a URL, an email address, a key, or names, figures or
text copied from the task that the user may not want shared. When need_search is false, queries is [].


Reply with only one JSON object that matches this JSON schema, nothing else:
{"properties": {"rationale": {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}], "description": "optional, at most two sentences"}, "need_search": {"type": "boolean"}, "why": {"type": "string"}, "queries": {"items": {"properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}, "reason": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["query", "reason"], "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false}, "type": "array"}}, "required": ["rationale", "need_search", "why", "queries"], "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false}
